title: MASSIVE Demand for “Dirt-Cheap” US Corn – Mexico, Colombia, South Korea Load Up

bullets: Corn: 2.9 mmt (113 mil bu), the highest of the marketing year. Mexico was the top buyer. Total sales so far are down 28% from last year
Beans: 1.2 mmt (42 mil bu), down 21% from the prior week. China was the top buyer. Total sales so far are up 78% from last year
Wheat: 182.8k mt (7 mil bu), the lowest of the marketing year and below expectations. Mexico led. Total sales so far are down 28% from last year
Friday flash sales: corn 330k mt to Mexico. Beans 134k mt to China, 120k mt to Vietnam, 100k mt to unknown
Trump, Putin and Xi hold their first three-way meeting Thursday at APEC in Shenzhen, plus a Trump–Xi one-on-one
China is close to its 25 mmt US soybean target but well behind on its $17B commitment for other US farm goods
Jan27 beans up about 13¢ on the week to ~$12.32 (+3.2%), on tighter US supply and strong demand
Wheat higher on Black Sea shipping problems
Ukrainian drone strikes crippled Russia’s southern grain ports. October seaborne exports fell 56% to 2.8 mmt, and Baltic/Arctic routes aren’t making up the gap
Conab cut Brazil’s wheat crop to 5.26 mmt from 5.73 (El Niño hurt yield and quality) and raised imports to 8.94 mmt. Corn and soy estimates unchanged
The Brazil weather segment (at 20:14) isn’t covered because there’s no transcript
The Jones Act waiver is extended 90 days, so foreign-flagged ships can keep moving fuel, fertilizer and soyoil between US ports. Domestic shipbuilders oppose it
